anya: FYI rolling canary for the new 4-bit runtime started at 21:00 UTC. small percentage traffic -> default NF4 kernels.
sam: saw an alert, large mem spike on a few hosts around 21:12. trace attached below. :eyes:
dario: dropping throughput by ~18% on sequence lengths >1024? thats odd given expected win from 4-bit.
maya: stack: inference-runtime v2.4.1 + quant-svc v0.9.3 (nf4 kernels). no other changes in deployment group.
profiling-bot: profiler run: run_profiler --host host-17 --duration 60s --events cpu,kernel,mem
profiling-bot: ```
# top slow paths (aggregated)
kv_cache::get_cached_prefix         42%  (syscalls high)
quant_kernels::matmul_4bit         28%  (high cross-shard memcpy)
batch_scheduler::make_batches       15%  (many tiny batches)
mem_alloc::fragmentation            10%  (heap overhead ~24GB)
``` 
anya: the kv_cache line is suspicious — many small cached entries and frequent evictions leads to fragmentation. we saw similar pattern in earlier long-context tests.
sam: can we get heap profiles? which allocator? jemalloc or tcmalloc?
dario: jemalloc. heap profile on host-17: "fragmented: 23.7GB, live: 5.2GB, rss: 32.1GB". shows a lot of short-lived allocations from batch assembly.
maya: why are we creating many tiny batches? batching heuristic changed to prefer latency SLOs; it now flushes when either tokens>=64 or requests>=4. during evening traffic we get lots of 1-2 request bursts so tokens cap triggers more flushes.
anya: so we have more flushes -> more tiny allocations -> kv cache churn -> freelist fragmentation -> mem spike -> OS pages pinned -> throughput drop. chain reaction.
sam: can we reproduce locally with loadgen? run: loadgen --pattern poisson --qps 250 --seq-len 1200 --model nf4
maya: did that, and reproduced memory cliff. repro note: disabling the new batching heuristic (revert to tokens>=256) eliminates fragmentation.
dario: interestingly, matmul_4bit spikes correlated with cross-device memcpy. seems our kernel picks the 4-bit path that uses sharded buffers and memcpy on every step. previous fp8 path did local compute.
anya: short-term mitigation: 1) set canary back to 0% 2) force fallback to 8-bit kernels for sequence length > 1024 3) revert batching heuristic to tokens>=256 for canary ring
sam: agreed. also enable jemalloc decay to aggressively purge: MALLOC_CONF="purge:decay"
maya: added a rollout bump to revert heuristic in canary: applied 1795123468 -> rollout-controller acknowledged.
profiling-bot: new profiler post-fix shows: ```
# top slow paths (aggregated) after revert
quant_kernels::matmul_4bit         12%  (reduced memcpy)
batch_scheduler::make_batches       6%  (fewer tiny batches)
mem_alloc::fragmentation            2%  (heap overhead ~4GB)
``` 
dario: perf numbers: throughput recovered +22%, p99 latency down from 420ms -> 310ms on the heavy hosts.
anya: longer term proposals: - kernel selector should prefer non-sharded 4-bit variant for long-context workloads - batching heuristic should include request-size histograms and dynamically pick token cap per host - make kv cache alloc strategy use slab allocator for prefix KV to avoid fragmentation
sam: one more: add telemetry to tag allocations that come from batch assembly so we can correlate in profiles (alloc_tag=batched_io). low-effort and helps root cause next time.
maya: filing a short RFC for the slab allocator + kernel selector change. will include microbenchmarks of both nf4 variants (sharded vs local) across sequence lengths.
anya: can we also run a calibration sweep? suspect calibration scale factors changed between quant-svc v0.9.2 -> v0.9.3 and could push kernels into the sharded path.
dario: scheduled calibration-run across 8 hosts starting 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC. will report metrics: throughput, mem_rss, memcpy_bytes/sec.
sam: thanks all. I'll keep the canary paused and monitor infra alerts. tagging infra-bot to keep automated remediation ready. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: remediation playbook step A executed: canary set to 0% (action id: cb-1795123499). monitoring window open for 30m.
anya: follow-up tasks assigned in thread: maya -> RFC, dario -> kernel perf microbench, sam -> infra knobs, anya -> telemetry tags. will sync tomorrow 10am PT.
maya: ack.
